newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cetes rates fall for first time in weeks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cetes rates fall for first time in weeks.

text.p: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fell slightly on Monday due to a steady peso, breaking five weeks of consecutive gains that had pushed rates sharply higher and bruised the country's financial markets.

Rates on the bellwether 28-day paper slipped four basis points to 29.85 percent, while rates at the longer-term fell slightly more. A Reuters survey of nine Cetes dealers earlier in the day forecast a fall of two basis points.
Analysts said it may be too early to tell whether rates have topped out for the short term and will continue to trend down in the coming weeks.

"The central bank and the market want relatively high real rates until they can confirm that exchange rate stability will last for awhile," said Sergio Martin, an economist at ING Barings in Mexico City.

The peso has steadied in the past two weeks after tumbling from about 7.55 to 8.0 per dollar during October in a long-awaited adjustment. On Monday, the benchmark 48-hour peso gained 0.3 centavos to 7.8920/7.8980 per dollar.
During the peso's slide, one-month Cetes rates soared from a low of 22.74 percent on October 8 to last week's high of 29.89 percent.

Mexico went through a similar bout of financial instability during the same time last year, when higher interest rates and a weaker peso finally attracted investors and allowed for rates to come back down and not hurt the peso.
The same thing may be happening this time around, analysts said.
"The demand reflects heightened investor interest, which paints a brighter picture for year end," a Mexico City analyst said.
At Monday's auction, demand for the auction as a whole was a healthy 14.15 billion pesos, some 4.29 times the amount on offer. The bid-to-cover ratio last week was 3.38 times.

While longer-term Cetes rates fell slightly more than the one-month paper, analysts said they expect the yield curve to remain inverted for the next few weeks due to inflation pressures in November and December.
The rate on three-month Cetes slipped 22 basis points to 29.30 percent, while the half-year paper fell 28 basis points to 27.70 percent.
Mexico held the weekly auction on Monday instead of Tuesday because of Wednesday's Revolution Day holiday.
